RETROSPECTIVE ARCHITECTURE DECISION · 11 OCTOBER 2026

ADR-0005: One local ACID business boundary

Status

Accepted; local harness transaction implemented, existing-service integration is pilot work

Context

Existing banking services own their interactions and business invariants. Governed export intent and audit must commit atomically with each participating business change.

Decision

Keep each participating business writer and its sovereignty hook/outbox within its existing local transaction. Co-locate modules only where a business invariant requires one local unit of work; estate-wide consolidation is not a prerequisite. Preserve independent services with explicit consistency or saga contracts. Remote copies remain asynchronous.

Alternatives

A synchronous distributed transaction across regions; a transaction per former microservice boundary.

Consequences

Regional service availability and latency avoid a WAN quorum on every business command. Remote projections can lag and need explicit read freshness and policy guards.

Evidence

poc/operational.py; poc/operational_schema.sql; design/src/operational_update.py

Gate

Rollback must include business and outbox rows; retry must not duplicate effects. Verify every governed writer and existing-service adapter separately; do not infer cross-service ACID or require Java consolidation.
